question: There are exactly \(K\) positive integers \(b\) with \(5\le b\le2024\) such that the base-\(b\) integer \(2024_b\) is divisible by \(16\) (where \(16\) is in base ten). What is the sum of the digits of \(K?\)
solution:
Expanding the base-\(b\) numeral and factoring gives
\[
2024_b=2b^3+2b+4=2(b+1)(b^2-b+2).
\]
Thus \(16\mid2024_b\) exactly when \(8\mid P\), where \(P=(b+1)(b^2-b+2)\). We only need to check the eight possible remainders of \(b\) modulo \(8\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrr}
b\bmod8&0&1&2&3&4&5&6&7\\
P\bmod8&2&4&4&0&6&4&0&0
\end{array}
\]
Therefore the successful bases are exactly those congruent to \(3,6,\) or \(7\) modulo \(8\).

Since \(2024=253\cdot8\), the integers from \(1\) through \(2024\) form \(253\) blocks of eight consecutive integers. Each block contains one integer in each remainder class, so there are \(253\cdot3=759\) successful integers in that range. Of these, only \(3\) is below the required minimum of \(5\). Hence
\[
K=759-1=758,
\qquad 7+5+8=\boxed{20}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
